title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Abolishing Certain Judicial Interpretations Issued Between 1979 and 1989

articles.content_en:
December 31, 1996 Fa Fa [1996] No. 34

To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

After publishing the first batch of the catalogue of judicial interpretations to be abolished, our Court promptly commenced a comprehensive review of judicial interpretations issued between 1979 and 1989. We now issue to you the second batch of the catalogue of judicial interpretations decided to be abolished upon discussion by the Adjudication Committee of our Court. This batch consists of 69 judicial interpretations to be abolished, including 16 in the area of criminal adjudication, 34 in civil adjudication, and 19 in economic adjudication. Among them, a few documents were issued in the form of "letters" or "replies." Considering that these documents possessed the nature of judicial interpretations and at the time served to guide adjudicative work, in the spirit of respecting history and maintaining the original form, they are also included in this clearance as judicial interpretations. The abolished judicial interpretations shall no longer be applied as of the date hereof (some have already ceased to have effect on their own). However, judgments and rulings made in relevant cases previously applying the aforesaid judicial interpretations shall remain valid. The work of clearing judicial interpretations shall continue. Where judicial interpretation documents jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court and relevant departments need to be abolished, our Court shall jointly issue a document with the relevant departments to abolish them. For those judicial interpretations in which only part of the content is no longer suitable for current adjudicative practice, they are not included in this clearance; our Court shall, on the basis of comprehensive clearance, organize relevant departments to study and revise them. All localities shall promptly report any comments to our Court.

Catalogue of Judicial Interpretations Issued between 1979 and 1989 Decided to be Abolished by the Supreme People's Court (Second Batch)

(Adopted upon discussion at the 869th Meeting of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court)
